out:
{
  "hypothesis": "Predicted that neuroticism would be associated with individual differences in surface-based morphometry measures in prefrontal and temporal areas, that extraversion would correlate with surface-based morphometry metrics in the prefrontal cortex, and that conscientiousness would be linked to variations in cortical anatomy in prefrontal and parietal regions.",
  "design": "correlational",
  "manipulation_or_predictor": "Five-Factor Model personality traits (neuroticism, extraversion, openness, agreeableness, conscientiousness) assessed via the NEO-Five-Factor-Inventory.",
  "outcome_measure": "Surface-based morphometry measures including cortical thickness, surface area, cortical volume, and local gyrification index derived from structural MRI scans.",
  "population_and_setting": "Healthy young adult participants drawn from the Human Connectome Project public dataset in the United States.",
  "sample_size_total": 507,
  "recruitment_and_incentive": "Public dataset from the Human Connectome Project (WU-Minn Consortium and MGH-USC HCP).",
  "analysis_plan": "Vertex-by-vertex cluster analysis using a multivariate general linear model (GLM) correlating subject-specific surface-based morphometry measures at each vertex with individual personality scores, including age, total intracranial volume, and sex as covariates, with cluster correction via Monte Carlo simulation.",
  "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "not stated",
  "other_methods_notes": "Structural MRI scans were acquired using a 3-Tesla Siemens Skyra unit. Pre-processed structural data were obtained using FSL, FreeSurfer, and Connectome Workbench suites."
}
